proof: Through Core with a signed registry and a repository that declares a check, the compiler enumerates single-slot and continuation plans, prevalidates all of them, selects the best hard-eligible plan at cold start as QUALITY_FLOOR_INFEASIBLE with every candidate's missing evidence named, produces the same plan id, input digest and candidates for identical inputs, narrows to a manual pin and refuses an ineligible one, compiles nothing under a cap that fits no plan while the plan in force stays, and admission refuses a continuation the plan does not declare. Synthetic registries prove stale statistics, insufficient cap, price overflow, disallowed residency, unavailable assurance and a revoked pin are refused or excluded with reasons, and that expected cost prefers a mini-plus-continuation plan over a plain stronger solver.
audit: PARTIAL before this task: admission and feasibility existed, but nothing enumerated the plans a request could run; the direct plan was the only compiled plan.
limitations: Nothing executes a compiled plan yet (EPR-005/006). Reviewer and reviser slots are not enumerated until EPR-018 enforces reviewer isolation, so the reviewer canonical-write injection has nothing to inject into. expected_input_tokens (40000) and delta (0.05) are fixed in Core and part of the digest. gate_version is gate-1 and risk_version is none because no gate or risk model exists yet.
